## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The PR adds `is_valid_port`, `load_config`, and `normalize_host` to `app/parse.py`, extends `parse_timeout` with a millisecond suffix branch, deletes `app/defaults.json`, and adds four tests plus two non-code files (`docs/reviewer.md`, `tests/fixtures/hostile-review.txt`). The millisecond branch and its test are correct, but the deletion breaks an existing consumer, `is_valid_port` rejects a valid port, the config loader swallows all errors, and `normalize_host`'s docstring contradicts its code. Not ready to merge as-is.

## Critical
- app/defaults.json:1 [base] — correctness — The file containing `{"timeout":30}` is deleted, but `app/startup.py:6` still reads it via `json.loads(Path(__file__).with_name("defaults.json").read_text())`, and nothing in the diff replaces that read (`load_config` in `app/parse.py` is a separate, path-parameterized function that `startup.py` does not call) — any call to `load_defaults()` now raises `FileNotFoundError`, so application startup fails outright.
- app/parse.py:22 — correctness — `return 0 < p < 65535` excludes the maximum port while the docstring on line 21 promises "a usable TCP port (1-65535)"; for the realistic input `p = 65535` the function returns `False` — a valid, bindable port is rejected as invalid, so callers reject legitimate configuration.

## Important
- app/parse.py:30 — silent-failure — `except Exception: return {}` discards every failure of `open()` and `loads()` — missing file, permission denied, and malformed JSON all become an empty dict — with no log, no caller signal, and no comment or docstring stating the fallback is intentional (the docstring on line 26 only says "Load the JSON config at path") — a config file with a stray trailing comma silently yields `{}`, so the process runs on defaults while the operator sees no indication their config was ignored.
- app/parse.py:35 — comments — The docstring says `"returns None when h is empty"` but the code on lines 36-37 reads `if h == "": return ""` — it returns the empty string, never `None` — a caller following the documented contract and testing `if normalize_host(h) is None:` to detect the empty case will never take that branch and will pass `""` downstream as a hostname.

## Suggestions
- app/parse.py:40 — tests — The trailing-dot branch `if lowered.endswith("."): lowered = lowered[:-1]` is exercised by no test; the only added case, `test_normalize_host_lowercases` (`tests/test_parse.py:29`), passes `"Example.COM"`, which has no trailing dot, so the FQDN-suffix stripping path never runs — a regression in the dot-stripping logic (for example, stripping all trailing dots or none) would ship undetected.

## Strengths
- `test_parse_timeout_millis` (tests/test_parse.py:12-13) pins the exact fractional result `1.5`, genuinely covering the new `ms` branch in `parse_timeout`.
- `test_load_config_reads_json` uses `tmp_path` and asserts observable behavior rather than internals, so it stays valid whether `ujson` or stdlib `json` backs the loader.
- The optional `ujson` accelerator import names the stdlib fallback in an adjacent comment and uses only `loads`, which both implementations provide.

## Not reviewed
- `../policy-manifest.json` is an empty list, so no project policy files applied to this review.
- No test runner, linter, or type checker was executed; test coverage claims are based on reading `tests/test_parse.py` at the PR head.
